app.subtitle: OSINT workstation for KAS analysts: linking public web traces to crypto addresses
app.footer: Results are analytical premises, not a ruling. Data in demonstration cases is synthetic.
app.notFoundBody: The address is wrong or the case was removed.

cases.title: Cases
cases.lead: A case holds the identifiers of one person and the successive analyses of those identifiers.
cases.loadDemoAddress: Demonstration: who is behind an address?
cases.demoHint: The demonstration case contains synthetic data only (the person "Jan Testowy").
cases.emptyBody: Create a case with your own identifiers or load the demonstration case. All its data is synthetic.

form.title: New case
form.lead: Give at least one identifier. The system searches the selected sources, recognises crypto addresses and rates how likely each is linked to the person.
form.identifiersHint: The more different identifiers you give, the firmer the links: independent sources confirm each other.
form.sourcesHint: By default only the synthetic "mini-internet" is searched. Live sources send requests outside the system, so tick them deliberately.

connectorNotes.sandbox: Pages, profiles, adverts and addresses are all artificial. Recommended for demonstrations.
connectorNotes.github: A user's profile and profile README; with a token also address search in code. Requests go to github.com.
connectorNotes.wayback: Earlier copies of pages on which addresses were found: which address was on the page and when (date of the copy). Pages of the synthetic internet are looked up in its own archive, others at archive.org.
connectorNotes.gravatar: Public Gravatar profile: name, verified accounts; crypto wallets only with GRAVATAR_API_KEY (without a key they are skipped, with a note). E-mails on reserved domains (example.org etc.) are answered only by the synthetic mini-internet.
connectorNotes.ens: Address ↔ ENS name and text records (com.github, com.twitter, email, url) through a public RPC node. A reverse record counts only when the name resolves back to the same address.

form.chainLiveNote: Needs API keys in the .env file. Sources without a key are skipped with a message.
form.submitRun: Create the case and run the analysis

errors.title: Enter a case name.
errors.identifiers: Add at least one identifier with a value.
errors.connectors: Select at least one data source.

identifierHints.NAME: The weakest link (−20 pts): needs confirmation by another identifier.
identifierHints.NICK: A forum or portal nick. The same nick on another platform may belong to someone else.
identifierHints.MESSENGER: A messenger handle, e.g. @name. Treated as a declared contact.
identifierHints.SOCIAL_LOGIN: A login on a social or developer service.
identifierHints.EMAIL: An exact e-mail match adds 10 pts.
identifierHints.ADDRESS: BTC, ETH, TRON or an ENS name. The system shows who published this address.

case.noRuns: This case has not been analysed yet.
case.scheduleHint: The program repeats the analysis by itself with the settings of the last one (sources, blockchain mode) and compares it with the previous one.

demoChange.title: Demo: change at a source
demoChange.original: The synthetic mini-internet is in its original state. Run the analysis, simulate the change, then run it again — you will see the differences and notifications.
demoChange.changed: The personal page of persona A now shows a NEW (synthetic) address. Run the analysis again: the comparison, notifications and section 8 of the report appear.

run.failed: The analysis ended with an error

searched.title: Sources searched
searched.summaryEmpty_one: Searched {{count}} source — no crypto addresses found.
searched.summaryEmpty_other: Searched {{count}} sources — no crypto addresses found.
searched.summaryNothing: None of the selected sources looks up the kinds of identifier given — nothing was searched.

round.2: addresses found in the sources: who else publishes them ({{queries}})
round.3: accounts that published the address: their other traces ({{queries}})
round.4: earlier copies of the pages with addresses in the web archive ({{pages}})

outcome.UNSUPPORTED: this source does not look up this kind of identifier

links.empty: There are no links to assess in this run.
links.emptyHint: Rejected attributions are in their own tab.
links.selectHint: Select a row to see how the score is built.

decision.title: Analyst's decision
decision.note: The decision is stored separately and never changes the computed score.

rejected.title: Rejected attributions
rejected.lead: These addresses are not attributed to the person (0%): they belong to an exchange, a service or a contract, or are a known fundraising or example address. The interaction with them is recorded and can be a lead, e.g. contact with an exchange is grounds for a KYC request.

address.title: Address card
address.noLabels: No label: the address is treated as unhosted.
address.publishedNote: Source fact: the text around the address (±200 characters).
address.onchainNote: Calculated from the transaction history; PLN amounts use the NBP mid rate of the last business day before the transaction.
address.noChain: No blockchain data for this address.
address.noChainWhy: In "{{mode}}" mode only the demonstration personas' addresses, or addresses with an available source, have a history.
address.cashOutDetected: Flows to points where funds can leave the crypto market were detected.
address.unvalued: Items not valued: {{count}} (no rate or price).
address.truncated: History cut to the latest page returned by the provider.
address.partialValuation: partial: some transfers have no valuation

tags.TO_AD_ADDRESS: to an address from an advert

graph.title: Link graph
graph.lead: Identifiers, addresses, sources and counterparties. Grey dashed lines are excluded attributions. Click an element to see its details.

legendItems.address: Address; outline colour is the score band
legendItems.counterparty: Blockchain counterparty; colour shows the type
legendItems.linked: Link; the label is the score
legendItems.transfer: Flow; the label is the value in PLN

graph.selectHint: Select an element of the graph to see its details.

evidence.title: Sources and evidence
evidence.lead: Each piece of evidence has a URL, a fetch time and the SHA-256 of the full content. The database keeps only a snippet (data minimisation).
evidence.author: Author
evidence.aiHint: Generated by a local model — to be verified. It does not change the score.

identities.title: Who is behind the address
identities.lead: Accounts that published the address, and the other addresses of those accounts. The same nick on another platform does not prove it is the same person.

relation.SAME_NICK_OTHER_PLATFORM: same nick on another platform; possibly another person

identities.empty: No account that published this address was found.

notes.CHAIN_KEY_MISSING: The {{key}} key is missing from .env — lookups on {{chain}} are disabled.
notes.NBP_HTTP: PLN valuation unavailable: the NBP server returned HTTP error {{status}}.
notes.NBP_NO_RATE: PLN valuation unavailable: no NBP {{currency}} rate before {{day}}.
notes.HISTORY_TRUNCATED: History truncated to the last page returned by the provider.
notes.UNVALUED_TRANSFERS: Transfers without a valuation: {{count}} (no stablecoin or price source).
notes.EGRESS_BLOCKED: Connection to host {{host}} blocked: it is not on the allowlist.
notes.GRAVATAR_WALLETS_SKIPPED: Gravatar: crypto wallets skipped — no {{key}} in the .env file (the profile was read).
notes.AI_UNAVAILABLE: The local AI model is unavailable ({{detail}}) — the analysis ran without AI suggestions.

report.polishOnly: The report is written in Polish. The PDF and JSON contain the same data as this view.

audit.title: Request log
audit.lead: Every request the program sent to an outside service: when, for which case, where to and with what result. The log holds neither response content nor query parameters.

changes.title: Changes since the previous run
changes.first: This is the first analysis of this case — nothing to compare with.
changes.none: No changes since the analysis of {{date}}: same addresses, same scores, no new transactions.
changes.differentSources: The analyses used different sources or blockchain mode — some differences may come from that.
changes.sourceChanges: Address changed on the same source

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty: No notifications. They appear when a later analysis of a case finds a change.
notifications.NEW_ADDRESS: New address {{chain}} {{address}} with a score of {{score}}%.
